newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-PRASAD TAKES 3-40 AS SOUTH AFRICA COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PRASAD TAKES 3-40 AS SOUTH AFRICA COLLAPSE.

text.p: Indian seamer Venkatesh Prasad captured three wickets as South Africa slumped to 142 for five at tea on the opening day of the first test at Kingsmead on Thursday.
Prasad picked up the key wickets of Daryll Cullinan (1) and captain Hansie Cronje (15) for overall figures of three for 40 while fellow pacemen Javagal Srinath and David Johnson took a wicket apiece.

South Africa, who had recovered well during the morning session after the early loss of opener Gary Kirsten for two, slid from 70 for one at lunch to 113 for five by the 44th over on a blameless pitch.
Opener Andrew Hudson, who survived a sharp chance off Srinath on 39, provided the only batting resistance for the home side during the afternoon.
Although decidedly shaky during the first hour of play when the ball was swinging around, Hudson soon settled into his positive front-foot game.
He reached his 50 with his eighth four in 118 deliveries and, by tea, was unbeaten on 70 with all-rounder Brian McMillan 10 not out.
Earlier, Adam Bacher, who had played without blemish during a partnership of 62 for the second wicket with Hudson, departed for 25 two overs after lunch.
Playing half forward defensively, he was adjudged leg before to a Srinath off-cutter, having faced 73 deliveries and struck three fours and a hooked six.
Cullinan fell in the very next over. Shuffling across his crease, he edged a Prasad delivery through to wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia and South Africa were in trouble at 71 for three.
Cronje followed in similar fashion 10 overs later, edging Prasad behind as he pushed half forward.
Herschelle Gibbs was then dismissed for no score cutting loosely at a Johnson delivery to give wicketkeeper Mongia his third catch of the innings.
